title: Microbial necromass outweighs lignin in contributing to soil recalcitrant carbon accumulation during vegetation restoration in a subtropical karst region
content:
Our study expands the traditional lignin-centric theoretical framework of carbon accumulation and emphasizes that the unique geochemical environment of karst regions facilitates a synchronous accumulation of bacterial and fungal necromass, jointly promoting stable SOC sequestration. We therefore propose that restoration strategies for karst-degraded ecosystems should focus on fostering active soil microbial communities while introducing plant species that facilitate soil calcium enrichment to enhance microbial carbon sequestration potential and promote the long-term preservation of SOC.


Abstract

Vegetation restoration is an important global strategy to enhance ecosystem resistance and promote soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. However, under this strategy, the mechanism underlying soil recalcitrant organic carbon (ROC) accumulation, particularly the relative contributions of plant- versus microbial-derived carbon, remains insufficiently explored. Using a space-for-time substitution approach, we selected three land-use types (cropland, shrubland and secondary forest) to represent a vegetation restoration chronosequence in karst regions of southwest China. We quantified soil lignin and microbial necromass carbon (MNC) by employing biomarker technologies (lignin phenols and amino sugars) and combined these measurements with ROC to assess relative contributions of plant versus microbial residues to stable SOC accumulation. Across the three land-use types, ROC accounted for more than 60% of total SOC pool. Vegetation restoration significantly increased soil ROC content by 193%, indicating that this strategy improved SOC stability and benefited long-term preservation of soil carbon. While both lignin and MNC contents significantly increased during vegetation restoration, MNC was identified as the key predictor of soil ROC accumulation. Soil MNC accumulation in shrublands and secondary forests was strongly associated with increased soil carbon and nitrogen availability and mineral protection (exchangeable calcium+magnesium and free and short-range ordered iron+aluminium oxides). Concurrently, higher substrate availability and mineral protection also facilitated soil lignin preservation. Importantly, fungal and bacterial necromass contributed almost equally to ROC accumulation. This phenomenon likely stemmed from the improvement in soil pH during vegetation restoration, which alleviated acid stress on bacterial proliferation. Synthesis and applications: Our study expands the traditional lignin-centric theoretical framework of carbon accumulation and emphasizes that the unique geochemical environment of karst regions facilitates a synchronous accumulation of bacterial and fungal necromass, jointly promoting stable SOC sequestration. We therefore propose that restoration strategies for karst-degraded ecosystems should focus on fostering active soil microbial communities while introducing plant species that facilitate soil calcium enrichment to enhance microbial carbon sequestration potential and promote the long-term preservation of SOC.

摘要

植被恢复是提升生态系统稳定性、促进土壤有机碳(SOC)固存的全球性重要策略。然而，在该策略下，土壤难分解有机碳(ROC)的累积机制，尤其是植物与微生物源碳的相对贡献，仍未得到充分探索。 本研究采用空间代替时间法，选取3种土地利用类型(包括农田、灌丛、次生林)以表征我国西南喀斯特地区植被恢复的不同时间阶段。借助生物标志物技术(木质素酚类和氨基糖)，本研究量化了土壤木质素与微生物残体碳(MNC)含量，并将二者与ROC库相结合，从而评估植物与微生物残体对稳定性SOC累积的相对贡献。 在三种土地利用方式下，ROC占总SOC库的60%以上。植被恢复促使土壤ROC含量显著增加193%，说明该策略可提高SOC稳定性并有助于土壤碳的长期固存。虽然木质素与MNC含量均在植被恢复过程中显著增加，但仅有MNC被确认为土壤ROC累积的关键预测因子。在灌丛与次生林中，土壤MNC的累积与土壤碳、氮有效性及矿物保护作用(交换性钙+镁和游离态及短程有序铁+铝氧化物)的提升密切相关。同时，较高的底物有效性与矿物保护作用也促进了土壤木质素的保留。重要的是，本研究发现，真菌残体与细菌残体对土壤ROC累积的贡献几乎处于同等水平。这一现象很可能源自植被恢复过程中土壤pH的改善，从而缓解了酸对细菌繁殖的胁迫作用。 综合与应用:本研究拓展了传统以木质素为核心的碳累积理论框架，并强调喀斯特地区独特的地球化学环境可促进细菌与真菌残体的同步累积，进而共同促进稳定SOC固存。因此，本研究指出:基于喀斯特退化生态系统的植被恢复策略应注重培养活跃的土壤微生物群落，同时引入有助于土壤钙富集的植物物种，以增强微生物碳固存潜力，促进SOC的长期保存。
